subtopic: Moving abroad or to a new city
passage:
Charu: just landed!! my flat is empty and the SIM shop closes soon 😅
Rekha: breathe. Take the tram to the mall, there's a shop by the pharmacy. I'll send the exact stop
Rekha: also come Saturday, we're cooking for Ugadi, bring nothing
Charu: really? thank you, I was dreading the first weekend 🥺
Rekha: same when I came. Someone did this for me, so now I do it for you
Charu: what about my colleagues? they keep inviting me to trivia night
Rekha: go!! I love our group but I don't want to only ever go to the dinners from home. trivia sounds fun
Charu: ok. trivia Thursday, Ugadi Saturday
Rekha: perfect. and next year you'll help the next newcomer 🙂

qa.q: What is Rekha's group cooking for on Saturday?
How does Charu feel about the first weekend, and what changes it?
qa.a: Charu was dreading the first weekend, and feels relieved and grateful when Rekha invites Charu to cook for Ugadi.

qa.q: How can Charu enjoy the group from home and still avoid living in a bubble?
qa.a: Go to the Ugadi cooking on Saturday and also say yes to the colleagues' trivia night on Thursday.

qa.q: Why might Rekha push Charu toward trivia night instead of only the group dinners?
qa.a: Rekha loves the group but does not want to only ever go to the dinners from home, and wants Charu to mix with colleagues too rather than stay in a bubble.

grounding: People from your region are a lifeline; enjoy it but mix with the wider community, and pay forward the help you got to the next newcomer.
